newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar closes well bid.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar closes well bid.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed well bid after a busy trading session on Wednesday and dealers said they expect it to trade higher.
The Kiwi had encountered "speculative selling" as it had on Tuesday but Japan's "tankan" report was the catalyst for dollar bloc buying, including the New Zealand dollar.
It ended at US$0.6926/33 compared with its 0.6911/18 opening while the Trade-Weighted Index closed at 65.59 from 65.46.
The Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan corporate survey confirmed only a slow pace of economic recovery there and that was the excuse to buy dollar currencies, dealers said.
The market had been testing the downside in the Kiwi for the past two days but good local buying interest plus the stronger Australian dollar caught traders off guard.

"Dips are so short-lived in the Kiwi, there is so much demand out there on the back of the euros, samurais and the yield in particular, that it is really going to take a political shock to get the Kiwi down," a Wellington dealer said.
New Zealand holds a general election on October 12.
